subject: mathematics
question_text: Define the trace of a matrix. Find the trace of the matrix with rows (1, 3, −5), (2, −1, 5) and (2, 0, 1).

recall_prompt: Say what the trace of a matrix is and how you would find it here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Define the trace
steps.margin_note: First mark, and half the question — it says "define", so the definition must be written even though the number is easy.
lines: The trace of a square matrix is the sum of the

recall.must_convey: That the trace is the sum of the elements on the principal (main) diagonal of a SQUARE matrix.
accept: the trace is the sum of the elements in the principal diagonal of a square matrix
trace means adding up the main diagonal entries
it is the sum of the diagonal elements
trace ante principal diagonal lo unna elements sum
add the entries running from top left to bottom right

steps.why: The word "define" is worth a mark on its own. A correct number with no definition answers only half of what was asked.
common_mistakes: Giving the number and skipping the definition.
Defining it as the sum of ALL the elements.

steps.label: Add the diagonal
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The principal diagonal is 1, −1, 1 — top-left to bottom-right. Nothing off that line is used.

recall.must_convey: That the diagonal entries 1, −1 and 1 are added to give a trace of 1.
accept: the diagonal is one minus one and one so the trace is one
add one minus one plus one to get one
one minus one plus one equals one, trace one

steps.why: The principal diagonal runs top-left to bottom-right. The other diagonal has no name in this course and is not used.
common_mistakes: Adding every element of the matrix.
